case_name: State of Himachal Pradesh v Raj Kumar
respondent:
Raj Kumar
Supreme Court of India

8 January 2018
Criminal Appeal No. 31 of 2018, (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 1204 of 2015)
The Judgment was delivered by : R. Banumathi, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. This appeal preferred by the State challenges the judgment of the High Court of Himachal Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No.559 of 2008 acquitting the respondent under Section 302 IPC by setting aside his conviction and the sentence of life imprisonment imposed upon him by the trial court.
3. Husband of deceased Meena Devi passed away about eleven years ago prior to the incident. Meena Devi was residing with her son Jeewan Lal (PW-1), daughter Rekha Devi (PW-2) and accused Raj Kumar (brother-in-law) in the joint family house. On 23.08.2007 at 08.30 p.m., while Meena Devi was taking meal along with her family, respondent-accused came there in drunken condition and started abusing Meena Devi and her children PW-1 and PW-2 without any reason and threatened to kill them. Bar
facts: The case involves the murder of Meena Devi, who was found hanging from a pine tree in a nearby forest.
Meena Devi was living with her children and brother-in-law Raj Kumar in a joint family house.
On August 23, 2007, Raj Kumar came home drunk and threatened to kill Meena Devi and her children.
Jeewan Lal, Meena Devi's son, heard his mother's cries and saw Raj Kumar taking her towards the house of another accused, Om Prakash.
The next day, Jeewan Lal and Anant Ram, their maternal uncle, went to the police station to report Meena Devi missing.
On August 25, 2007, Meena Devi's body was found hanging from a pine tree in the nearby forest.
An autopsy was conducted by Dr. Vivek Banyal, who concluded that Meena Devi died due to haemorrhagic shock caused by rupture of her spleen and anti-mortem injuries suggesting gagging.
issues: Whether the High Court erred in acquitting Raj Kumar based on circumstantial evidence.
Whether the prosecution proved its case beyond a reasonable doubt.
petitioner_arguments: The State argued that the High Court erred in acquitting Raj Kumar and that the prosecution had established its case beyond a reasonable doubt through circumstantial evidence.
respondent_arguments: Raj Kumar argued that the prosecution's case was based on unreliable witnesses, including Jeewan Lal, who made improvements to his version of events.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the High Court erred in acquitting Raj Kumar and that the prosecution had established its case beyond a reasonable doubt through circumstantial evidence.
The Court noted that the trial court had found Jeewan Lal, Meena Devi's son, to be a trustworthy witness, despite his improvements to his version of events.
holding: The Supreme Court allowed the State's appeal and set aside the High Court's acquittal of Raj Kumar.
Raj Kumar was convicted of Meena Devi's murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
